newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE WHEAT DOWN FURTHER AS RAIN CONTINUES TO FALL.
newsitem.headline: SFE WHEAT DOWN FURTHER AS RAIN CONTINUES TO FALL.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures fell further on Monday after further good falls of rain strengthened prospects for the current wheat crop.
January 1998 and March 1998 both traded down sharply, by A$7.00 and A$6.50 to A$188.00 and A$190.00 respectively.
A total of 40 contracts changed hands in moderately heavy trading.
Settlement prices mostly fell by about A$7.00 a tonne in nearer-term contracts.
Put options again attracted interest with three January 1998 trading at a A$195.00 strike price and a A$15.00 premium.
Gary Booth of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures said recent rain in Australia's southern and eastern grain belt raised the prospect of better yields than recently thought likely.
If rain continued to fall Sydney's significant premium over Chicago could begin to shrink, with SFE wheat possibly falling by up to A$10.00 a tonne.
SFE wheat futures were moved to afternoon from morning trading on Monday.
